Q1: A huge city fire. The date counter reads 2 Sept 1666 and the caption says 'The Great Fire'. Timber-framed houses burn, with thick smoke over the city and the river.
Q2: It begins in one small place. A baker's (Thomas Farriner, baker to the King) oven fire and sparks set a narrow street alight (frames 22-23). The fire then spreads along the north bank of the river to cover a big area over several days (2-5 Sept).
Q3: People flee on foot with bundles, pile belongings onto horse carts, and escape in rowing boats on the river (frames 48-50). Some crowds camp in open fields with tents and campfires (frames 72-73). Some men pull down houses with hooks and ropes to make firebreaks (frame 40), and a house is blown up (frame 68). Two men bury items in a garden (frames 69-70).
Q4: The huge Gothic church on the hill, shown on screen with a caption naming Old St Paul's, catches fire on 4 Sept. Its windows blaze, molten lead or fire runs down the walls and along the street, and it is gutted (frames 59-65). By frame 85 the ruins include a toppled statue.
Q5: It is rebuilt in red brick, with new brick houses going up (frames 95-96, 98-99). The caption says 'Rebuilding on the old streets', so the layout is the old street pattern, not a new plan (frames 83-90). Maps with Wren's plan are shown, but the new streets seem to follow the old ones.
Q6: A large white domed cathedral rises above the red roofs. The caption reads 'The dome rules the skyline' (1711), and '365 ft' flashes on screen. A tall column (the Monument) appears in several skyline shots, but I'm not sure which frame is which.
Q7: On 29 Dec 1940 the city is bombed (night raids, airships/planes over an empty street) and burns again, called 'the second great fire'. Firefighters work along the river and on rooftops. The dome of St Paul's survives, shown in a 1942 photo (frame 160) and circled in the 1938 frames. Large areas around it are destroyed. The map marks '160 killed'.
Q8: A modern 2026 city of glass and concrete towers and office blocks beside the river with bridges. The old domed cathedral is still visible among the skyscrapers (frames 176, 180-181). At night the city is lit by windows (frames 184-190). The film ends with a 'How this film was made' text card.
